teaser.text: Dell Technologies sells the tools that people and organizations use to do computing work. Its dollar begins as a sale of hardware or support, moves through suppliers and employees, and becomes profit and cash only as Dell delivers, finances, and collects.

blocks.heading: Where could Dell’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted forecast puts Dell below today’s $586.28 share price at every date. It reaches $513.55 in October 2027, $486.67 in October 2028 and $470.75 in October 2029, including dividends.

The weighted value is $513.55 in October 2027, a return of -12% including dividends. It is $470.75 in October 2029, a return of -18% including dividends. The bear case carries 30% probability. The base case carries 50%. The bull case carries 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Dell’s forecast?

paragraphs.text: Normal operating profit is $21.9 billion in October 2027, then moderates in the following years. The first-year figure reflects the guidance anchor after allowing for a GAAP-to-adjusted gap. Later moderation reflects lower AI growth, with storage and commercial PCs providing balance. The bear case starts at $19.4 billion and falls to $14.5 billion in 2028. The bull case starts at $25 billion and reaches $30 billion by 2029. The bear reflects delayed sites, lower margins and weak collections; the bull assumes faster shipments, repeat orders and operating leverage. Inventory nearly doubled to $21.290 billion by July, while receivables also rose, making both outcomes credible.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Dell really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow begins with cash from operations and subtracts capital spending. Dell’s own measure goes further by removing financing-receivable and leased-equipment effects. Stock compensation also matters economically, because paying employees with shares transfers ownership even when it is not a cash payment.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Dell?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, says how many dollars investors pay for one dollar of annual profit. A trailing P/E uses the last twelve months; a forward P/E uses an estimate of future profit. GAAP is the formal accounting rulebook, so GAAP earnings can differ from adjusted earnings. Dell’s FY27 GAAP earnings-per-share guidance is $24.37, but that fiscal period is not identical to every forward estimate. The lower forward P/E therefore depends on profits arriving.

dividend.title: Dell dividend: cash coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: Dell pays a growing dividend, but coverage depends on cash collection, financing, and AI execution.
dividend.opening: Dell pays dividends to shareholders, and its fiscal 2026 distributions were covered much better by free cash flow. Dell still depends on cash collection, borrowing, and customer financing because free cash flow has been volatile.
dividend.closing: The full Dell memo also covers Dell’s business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Dell pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Base dividends begin at $2.52 per share, rise to $2.77, and then reach $3.05. The first figure is declared guidance; later increases are set at 10%, below the latest 20% increase because financing and investment compete for cash. The bear holds the payout flat, while the bull extends 20% annual increases to $3.62. Free cash flow has been volatile, and ordinary quarterly free cash flow was only $986 million.

blocks.heading: Does Dell’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Fiscal 2026 covered distributions much better, but the rise in cash was not purely operating surplus because debt issuance supplied much of it. Dell Financial Services also lends to customers and leases them equipment. A customer can receive an expensive AI system while paying over several years, leaving Dell with a financing receivable rather than immediate cash. Dell may therefore need funding even after recording the sale.

blocks.heading: What has Dell guided for fiscal 2027?

paragraphs.text: On September 1, 2026, Dell raised its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast and its AI-server target. Fiscal 2027 ends in January 2027; it is Dell’s accounting year, not the calendar year. AI servers are computers configured for artificial-intelligence workloads, so this target says these expensive systems should become a major part of Dell’s sales.

blocks.heading: What were Dell's last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: The last eight quarters show sales accelerating from 24,366 in November 2024 to 46,971 in July 2026. A specialist follows shipments, configurations, prices and product categories separately before trusting the consolidated growth rate.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Dell's next results?

paragraphs.text: Dell expects to report its October-quarter results in late November 2026. Investors should compare revenue with consensus, then examine inventory and cash movement. Backlog can rise while shipments disappoint because customer readiness and component availability are uneven. The useful question is how much backlog became delivered equipment and then collected cash.

DFS requires a second clock. Investors should track originations alongside overdue payments, charge-offs and reserves. Dell’s principal charge-off rate was 0.2% in fiscal 2026, but that backward-looking result may not reveal the risk in a rapidly expanding portfolio.
